axes.name: Accessibility severity ladder (aggregation)
axes.definition: Ranks colour failures: Critical (body < 4.5, or text invisible under CVD); High (UI < 3); Medium (4.5-7, or hue-only distinction); Pass.

measurement.formula: Severity lookup; anti-aliasing margin: prefer >= 4.7 for normal text (wcag-rules.md:115)

axes.name: Accent chroma cap
axes.definition: Saturated accents vibrate on dark: OKLCH chroma of primary/secondary/tertiary <= 0.11 dark, <= 0.17 light (M3 tones 50-400 on dark).

measurement.formula: mean over 3 accents of max(0, 1 - max(0, C - cap)/0.10)

axes.scifin_reason: Sci-Fin accents (income green / expense red) on dark backgrounds.
axes.port_inputs: theme hex values

axes.name: Fill can carry its own label
axes.definition: The derived on-colour on the accent and primary fills must reach 4.5:1. Graded on the normal-text ladder because UI labels are body copy.

measurement.formula: contrast(on-X, X) >= 4.5 for X in {accent, primary}

axes.scifin_reason: Buttons, chips and FABs on Sci-Fin's primary/accent.
axes.port_inputs: Theme hexes or probe button fg/bg

axes.name: Body-text contrast floor
axes.definition: Body text on its own surface must reach 4.5:1, enforced as a hard constraint because a weighted average lets a 1.08:1 pair hide.

measurement.formula: contrast_ratio(text, surface) >= 4.5

axes.scifin_reason: Universal gate.

axes.name: Body text contrast band (not too low, not glaring)
axes.definition: Eye-strain: onSurface on background should sit in a band - 9.5-13:1 dark (APCA dark ceiling near Lc 90), 10-16:1 light - not maximal.

measurement.formula: band(x, lo, hi, falloff) = 1 inside, else max(0, 1 - dist/falloff)

axes.scifin_reason: Sci-Fin dark/light themes; long reading of transaction lists.

axes.name: Categorical colour-vision collapse
axes.definition: Within one categorical family (data series or status semantics, same theme, no foregrounds), flags pairs that are distinct normally but collapse under deuteranopia or protanopia.

inputs: family colours (name regex SERIES/STATUS, or a Kotlin colour list of 3 or more)
measurement.formula: If dE2000_normal >= 15 and dE2000_sim(kind) < 10 for kind in {deuteranopia, protanopia}, report a medium finding.

axes.scifin_reason: Income/expense and over/under-budget status colours and category palettes.

axes.name: Category/series colours separable, incl. under CVD
axes.definition: Chart series (Okabe-Ito set) and category stripes must stay distinguishable: closest pair dE2000, also after protan/deutan/tritan simulation, each >= 3:1 on the card surface.

measurement.inputs: series/category hex list + card surface per theme
measurement.formula: separation = min(1, min_pair_dE2000/20); constraint: every colour >= 3:1 on the lightest surfaceContainer of all light palettes and in sRGB; mnemo: min pairwise dE under each CVD simulation reported

axes.weighting: series: identity + separation; mnemo: report (tritan stripe collapse noted, mitigated by the mode word)
axes.validation: mnemo values from designkit simulate_cvd + delta_e_hex.

axes.name: Categorical colours too similar
axes.definition: Within a categorical family, flags the worst pair under dE2000 10, which reads as the same colour to anyone. One finding per family.

measurement.formula: min pairwise dE2000 < 10 -> finding (worst pair named, plus a count of others)

axes.scifin_reason: Spending-category tag colours.

measurement.formula: For each element coloured with a status/up/down token: there is a glyph, sign (+/-) or text label inside or adjacent

axes.name: Headroom above contrast floors
axes.definition: Palettes sitting exactly on the floor are brittle; reward margin above the worst real pair.

measurement.inputs: scheme model in both lerp spaces, all non-advisory pairs
measurement.formula: worst = min over pairs of ratio/threshold (cap 9); headroom = clamp((worst - 1)/0.25, 0, 1)

measurement.formula: contrast(sim(fg,k), sim(bg,k)) >= threshold for k in {deut, prot, trit}

measurement.formula: floored min dE wf, scored CVD min dE ws; score = 0.5*clamp((wf-10)/(30-10)) + 0.5*clamp(ws/30); fail if wf < 10

axes.name: Find (items inspected in a launcher)
axes.definition: Expected items inspected to find a uniformly chosen feature in the ⊞ sheet: groups read one by one unless each is a filled hue region and G <= 6 (pop-out), then items one by one.

measurement.formula: pick = 1 if pop-out else (G+1)/2; within = (n+1)/2 (flat/cards) or folder/row variants; find = mean(pick + within)

axes.validation: Assumption stated (Treisman & Gelade 1980; Healey 1996); hue on text headings alone not counted.
axes.scifin_reason: Category grid in Add; Sci-Fin may not have a launcher.
axes.port_inputs: static group structure

axes.name: Hue group cohesion
axes.definition: How tightly hues cluster on the template's positions (the third CHA signal).

measurement.formula: max(0, 1 - mean(min angular dev to positions)/45)

axes.weighting: Scorer is registered (color.group_cohesion) but not in the default spec weights
axes.scifin_reason: Theme-level; optional.
axes.port_inputs: Theme hexes

axes.name: Hard-coded colours/strings/text sizes
axes.source: GlassCam_fixed/GlassCam/tools/critique/measure.py:174-183,225-236; mnemo critique.md:106 ('0 colour literals in screens')
axes.definition: Layouts should not hard-code colours (bypass themes), strings (bypass translation) or textSize in dp (ignores font scale); includes default vs locale string coverage.

measurement.formula: counts of #hex in layouts, literal text/hint/contentDescription, textSize in dp; it_coverage = (present - empty)/default * 100

axes.scifin_reason: Compose equivalents: Color(0x..) in screens, .sp outside Typography, literal strings; theme/palette switching in Sci-Fin depends on it.
axes.port_inputs: Kotlin source scan
sources: GlassCam_fixed/GlassCam/tools/critique/measure.py:174-183,225-236; mnemo critique.md:106 ('0 colour literals in screens')

axes.name: Hue harmony template match (Matsuda)
axes.definition: How well the chromatic roles' hues sit on one of eight Matsuda templates at a fitted base rotation, discounted when template slots are left empty.

inputs: hue per chromatic role (sat above threshold)
measurement.formula: For each base in hues: per hue dev = min angular distance to template positions; s = max(0, 1 - max(0, dev-10)/30); avg over hues * (occupied positions / positions), where a position counts as occupied if a hue is within 30 deg. Best over bases (harmony.py:87); best over templates with +0.01*len(offsets) tie-break (harmony.py:119).

constants.templates: monochromatic, analogous(+-30), complementary(180), split-complementary(150,210), triadic(120,240), tetradic(90,180,270), near-complementary, rectangle

axes.weighting: 0.40 of palette fitness (0.28 when refining; reduced on mobile)
axes.scifin_reason: Applies to Sci-Fin's theme tokens rather than per screen; most useful when comparing theme variants.
axes.port_inputs: Theme role hexes (primary, secondary, accent, surface, text) from the Kotlin theme or probe.

axes.name: Label/chip cost on rows
axes.definition: What tags/labels cost a row: extra height, wrapped lines, labels hidden behind +n, rows pushed below the bar, plus 'apart' cues that tell a label from the title without colour.

measurement.inputs: DOM probe of rows with labels
measurement.formula: extra_h = mean added height; lines = label lines beyond first; hidden = labels behind +n; rows_lost = rows pushed below bar vs no-label baseline; apart = count of cues (smaller text, dim ink, boundary, leading mark)

axes.aggregation: Pareto/rank sums in label_opt part A.
axes.scifin_reason: Category and tag chips on transaction rows.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON rows with chip bounds; baseline render without chips

axes.name: Adaptive icon safety (safe circle, opacity, palette, stroke)
axes.definition: An icon survives the launcher mask: ink inside the 66 dp safe circle, fully opaque art, dominant colours within dE2000 of the app lexicon, narrowest stroke >= 2 dp at 48 dp.

measurement.formula: % ink outside 72 dp circle (budget 2%) and 66 dp circle (budget 5%, BLOCK > 15%); alpha min == 255; nearest-lexicon dE ok < 10, warn < 18; percentile ink run -> dp ok >= 2, warn >= 1.2

axes.validation: ink defined by alpha for glyphs after RGB-distance gave 0.05 dp false readings
axes.scifin_reason: Only for the Sci-Fin launcher icon, not screens.
axes.port_inputs: icon PNG + theme lexicon

axes.name: Palette mood fit (model-judged)
axes.definition: An LLM judges whether the palette reads as the brief's mood words. It must not re-estimate harmony, contrast or distance.

measurement.formula: LLM 0..1; others x0.8

axes.scifin_reason: Could judge whether a theme variant reads 'calm and trustworthy' at the target register; low priority.
axes.port_inputs: Theme swatch PNG plus brief

axes.name: Pairwise hue harmony
axes.definition: Mean pairwise score of hue separations against the template's valid offsets. It ignores absolute position, unlike template match.

measurement.formula: For each hue pair: dev = min |sep - valid_offset| (valid offsets include 0); s = max(0, 1-dev/30); mean (harmony.py:69-85).

axes.scifin_reason: Theme-level, like template match.
axes.port_inputs: Theme hexes

axes.name: Visual comfort (no glare, no loud colours)
axes.definition: Large surfaces inside a lightness band (not pure white, not pure black), low surface chroma, and an accent below a 'no bright colours' chroma ceiling; owner ruled out glare and bright accents.

measurement.formula: mean of: mean surface score clamp(1 - outside_band/6); clamp(1 - (Cmax-0.02)/(0.06-0.02)); clamp(1 - (C_accent-0.10)/(0.167-0.10))

axes.validation: as palette_readability
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Calm-finance register fits; ceilings were tuned to this owner's taste and need Sci-Fin's own brand chroma.
axes.port_inputs: surface + accent hexes; Sci-Fin bands
axes.fit_reason: Calm-finance register fits; ceilings were tuned to this owner's taste and need Sci-Fin's own brand chroma.

axes.name: Palette fidelity (hue/saturation drift from seed)
axes.definition: How much of an existing palette's identity a candidate keeps. Only hue and saturation are scored, so lightness stays free to fix contrast.

measurement.formula: hue term per chromatic ref role (sat>=8): max(0, 1-drift/40); sat term per role: max(0, 1-|dS|/60); fidelity = 0.75*mean(hue) + 0.25*mean(sat).

axes.scifin_reason: Useful only when scoring theme variants against Sci-Fin's current palette.
axes.port_inputs: Current theme hexes as reference

axes.name: Palette fitness (aggregate, constraint-penalised)
axes.definition: Weighted palette score with device reweighting and a multiplicative penalty for violated constraints.

measurement.formula: fitness = sum(w*s); if infeasible: fitness *= 0.1^(number of violated constraints)

axes.scifin_reason: The penalty scheme (0.1^k) is a reusable pattern for Sci-Fin's own aggregate.
axes.port_inputs: Component scores

axes.name: Hue harmony template fit
axes.definition: How well the chromatic roles' hues fit the best harmony template (analogous, complementary, ...), via designkit harmony.best_template.

measurement.inputs: hues of primary/secondary/tertiary with HSL S > 0.08
measurement.formula: designkit harmony.best_template(hues) -> (template, fit)

axes.weighting: report (five skins analogous >= 0.95; one at 0.66 by design)
axes.scifin_reason: Descriptive only; useful when adding Sci-Fin palettes, not as a hard axis.
axes.port_inputs: theme hex values + designkit

axes.name: Surface layering
axes.definition: CIE L* steps along window -> nav -> card -> hover -> pressed compared with the design system's own steps: right direction, similar size, visible.

measurement.formula: per step: if ref ~0, 1 if |c| <= 3 else exp(-(|c|-3)/3); wrong direction 0; else exp(-ln(|c|/|f|)^2/(2*0.6^2)), scaled by |c|/1 if |c| < 1; mean of 4

axes.validation: as palette_readability
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Use Material 3 surfaceContainer tonal steps as the reference sequence.
axes.port_inputs: surface role hexes; M3 reference L* steps
axes.fit_reason: Use Material 3 surfaceContainer tonal steps as the reference sequence.

axes.name: Palette score: harmony, fidelity, separation
axes.definition: Weighted score per palette choice: harmony template fit 0.45, source fidelity 0.35, role separation 0.20 (capped at dE 25); personality levers (hue band, chroma, contrast spread, container lightness, gaps, scale) are design assumptions for the owner's three words.

measurement.formula: score = 0.45*harmony + 0.35*fidelity + 0.20*min(sep/25, 1)

axes.aggregation: Weighted (the only hand-weighted composite in the group).
axes.validation: Page reports what each lever produced so a word that did not show in the colours is visible.
axes.scifin_reason: Only if Sci-Fin picks palettes from a lexicon; needs designkit harmony templates.
axes.port_inputs: candidate palettes + source swatches

axes.name: Platform fit (Windows/Fluent)
axes.definition: How close neutrals sit to the platform's reference neutrals (mean dE2000) plus whether accent usage follows platform conventions (on-accent polarity, hover direction, focus ring = accent).

measurement.formula: 0.7*exp(-mean dE(12 neutral roles)/10) + 0.3*mean(polarity ok, clamp(dh/ref_dh), exp(-dE(focus,accent)/10))

axes.validation: as palette_readability
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Reference becomes Material 3 baseline / dynamic-colour neutrals on Android and Windows neutrals on desktop.
axes.port_inputs: role hexes; reference palette per platform
axes.fit_reason: Reference becomes Material 3 baseline / dynamic-colour neutrals on Android and Windows neutrals on desktop.

axes.name: Refinement constraints (hue anchor, fidelity budget)
axes.definition: When refining, the primary hue stays within 45 deg of the seed and no seeded role may move more than dE2000 15, unless the mode's lightness envelope forces it.

measurement.formula: hue_anchored: angular_distance(primary.hue) <= 45; fidelity_within_budget: per role dE2000(seed, candidate) <= 15, excluding forced moves (palette.py:209-277)

axes.scifin_reason: Only for theme-variant generation.
axes.port_inputs: Seed and candidate hexes

axes.name: Rendered colour census and chroma
axes.definition: Colours quantised to 16 levels per channel: how many occupy at least 0.5% of the render, dominant share, and mean and max Lab chroma of the top 24.

measurement.formula: significant = count(bins with share >= 0.005); mean_chroma = count-weighted mean of hypot(a,b) over top 24
measurement.direction: context-dependent (fewer and calmer for a low-tone register)

axes.scifin_reason: Mean chroma and saturated-area share give a computed 'alarm level' signal that can feed the register (red/amber at high tone, calm at low tone).
axes.port_inputs: PNG

axes.name: Rendered value structure
axes.definition: On the actual raster: how many of 5 luminance bands carry area, how dominant one band is, and whether the p5-p95 lightness range is flat.

measurement.formula: Downsample to 200px max; band share per 5 luma bands; occupied = shares >= 0.02; has_structure = occupied>=3 and max share < 0.8; flat = p95-p5 < 0.15

axes.weighting: error if flat, warn if thin
axes.scifin_reason: Runs on Sci-Fin PNGs unchanged. It was designed for illustrations, so the thresholds need recalibrating for UI (a light-theme screen is mostly one band).
axes.port_inputs: Screen PNG

axes.name: Rendered colour count and chroma
axes.source: mnemo_pass4/mnemo/tools/design_critique_2026_09_18/measure_shots.py:66 (craftkit imgstat._colour_report); GlassCam analyse.sh (designkit extract k-means, rendered vs declared drift)
axes.definition: How many colours the eye can distinguish on the render and how saturated they are; GlassCam compares the k-means palette on screen with the declared one.

measurement.formula: quantise RGB to 16 levels; significant = buckets >= 0.5% of pixels; mean_chroma = count-weighted Lab chroma of top 24 buckets; max_chroma

axes.scifin_reason: Check Sci-Fin category-colour sprawl on dashboards and rendered-vs-theme drift.
axes.port_inputs: PNG renders + declared theme
sources: mnemo_pass4/mnemo/tools/design_critique_2026_09_18/measure_shots.py:66 (craftkit imgstat._colour_report); GlassCam analyse.sh (designkit extract k-means, rendered vs declared drift)

axes.name: Reserved state colour cost
axes.definition: Reserving a hue for a state (done, due soon, attention) costs every lexicon colour within dE 15 of it; states themselves must be dE >= 20 apart (>= 10 under protan/deutan) and attention must have the set's highest chroma. Red forbidden.

measurement.formula: lost = count(lexicon colours within dE 15 of any reserved state); constraints as stated; ties to fewer reserved hues

axes.scifin_reason: Over-budget / overdue-bill colours vs category colours; red-free rule is Factotum-specific.
axes.port_inputs: state colour candidates + category palette

axes.name: Strong (full-contrast) targets / nav at full contrast
axes.definition: Tappable elements whose effective contrast against their nearest painted background is >= 7:1 (strong) and the subset in header/bar/rail (strong_nav): 'what the eye lands on first. Fewer = calmer, as long as the main action is among them.'

measurement.inputs: DOM via headless browser: [data-tap] elements, computed colour, opacity chain, nearest ancestor background with alpha > 0.5
measurement.formula: L_text_eff = L_text*opacity + L_bg*(1-opacity); ratio = (max+0.05)/(min+0.05); strong = count(ratio >= 7); strong_nav = count(ratio>=7 and inside .hdr/.bar/.rail)

axes.aggregation: strong_nav in T1 Pareto low-set; nav_glance 'primary' counted nav items at full strength (depth coding: 2-3).
axes.validation: T1.1 control (busy header) had strong_nav 5 vs 2 and lost.
axes.scifin_reason: Useful for keeping the money figure / Add the only loud things; needs the probe to give fg/bg colour per element instead of DOM.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON with element bounds, role (nav/action), text colour, resolved background colour and alpha

axes.name: Design-token adoption (coverage)
axes.definition: Token references divided by token references plus hard-coded literals across colour, spacing, type, radius, shadow and motion. It shows whether the system is adopted, not merely defined.

measurement.formula: coverage = uses/(uses+literals); literals inside token definitions are not counted; worst files ranked

axes.scifin_reason: Needs a Kotlin scanner: Color(0x..), .dp and .sp literals outside the theme versus MaterialTheme/LocalSpacing references. It scores code, not screens.
axes.port_inputs: Sci-Fin Kotlin source

axes.name: Token naming consistency, near-duplicates, orphans
axes.definition: A single naming convention, no colour/color spelling split, no colour tokens under dE2000 2.0 of each other (below the just-noticeable difference), and no defined-but-unused tokens.

measurement.formula: dominant convention among kebab/camel/snake, off-convention list; near_duplicate if dE2000 < 2.0 (dsaudit.py:271); orphan if 0 references incl. alias refs (dsaudit.py:295)

axes.scifin_reason: Codebase hygiene rather than a screen score; the near-duplicate check is easy to run on Sci-Fin's Kotlin colours via the designkit audit extractor.
axes.port_inputs: Kotlin theme tokens

axes.name: Type hierarchy clarity
axes.definition: Size-step separation from the modular scale ratio plus the heading-to-body weight contrast. Both are needed for levels to read as distinct.
axes.scifin_reason: Derive the effective ratio from the measured distinct sizes in a render (geometric-mean step), and the weights from the probe.
axes.port_inputs: Distinct font sizes and weights per role from the probe.

axes.name: Type-palette harmony
axes.definition: Contrast compliance of body and heading colours on the surface, plus alignment of the font pairing's aesthetic with the brief's mood.

measurement.formula: 0.6*mean(contrast_score(text), contrast_score(heading)) + 0.4*alignment. alignment: exact 1.0; 'any' 0.6; neighbour 0.5 (the reference fitness-signals.md:55 says 0.6); mismatch 0.2; unknown 0.6.

axes.scifin_reason: The contrast half is portable. The mood half depends on the skill's 21-pairing catalog, which does not describe Sci-Fin's fonts.
axes.port_inputs: Heading and body fg/bg from the probe; optionally Sci-Fin's own aesthetic tag mapped onto the neighbour graph.

axes.name: Typographic readability
axes.definition: Body line-height band, line measure in characters per line, and the WCAG contrast of body text on its surface.

measurement.formula: 0.4*LH + 0.3*measure + 0.3*contrast. LH: 1.0 in [1.5,1.7], 0.7 in [1.4,1.5) or (1.7,1.8], else 0.3. cpl = container_px/(base_px*0.5); measure: 1.0 in [50,75], 0.6 in [40,50) or (75,90], else 0.2. contrast: 1.0 >=7, 0.8 >=4.5, 0.4 >=3, else 0 (unknown palette -> 0.8).

axes.scifin_reason: Probes give the real font size, line height, container width and actual characters per line, so the 0.5em glyph estimate can be replaced. On a phone, 50-75 cpl is unreachable for most UI text, so the measure band should apply only to paragraph text.
axes.port_inputs: Per text node from the probe: font size (sp converted via density), line height, container width, measured characters per line, fg/bg colour.

axes.name: One style per kind of place
axes.definition: The same kind of place (colour token x position) never reads two ways.

measurement.inputs: text sites with colour token and position (first/row/later) and style
measurement.formula: sum over buckets weight_k/|styles_k| / total

axes.scifin_reason: Consistent style for every 'amount', every 'date', every 'category label' across screens.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON text nodes tagged by role

axes.name: Typography fitness (aggregate, medium-weighted)
axes.definition: Weighted sum of readability, hierarchy, palette harmony and rhythm, with weights shifted by medium.

measurement.formula: sum(w*score)

axes.scifin_reason: The dashboard weighting (readability 0.40) suits a tracker app opened repeatedly.
axes.port_inputs: Component scores

axes.name: Sprawl (craftkit ui findings)
axes.definition: Count of craftkit ui warnings plus off-grid spacing notes on the sheet alone, colour and contrast codes excluded ('nothing wins on colour' before the palette).

measurement.inputs: HTML page through creative-design-suite craftkit_cli ui --json
measurement.formula: count(findings with severity warn/error or code spacing-off-grid, code not starting colour/contrast)

axes.scifin_reason: Depends on craftkit parsing HTML/CSS; Compose renders are not HTML. A spacing-on-grid check from probe bounds could replace it.
axes.port_inputs: would need a probe-based 8 dp grid check instead

axes.name: Small-size legibility
axes.definition: Share of the full-size contrast range retained after box-filtering to 64 and 24 px. Tests whether a silhouette survives at icon size.

measurement.formula: retained = (p95-p5 at size)/(p95-p5 full); survives if >= 0.6

axes.scifin_reason: Only for the launcher icon, not screens.
axes.port_inputs: Icon PNG

axes.name: Contrast retained when downscaled
axes.definition: Share of full-size p5-p95 luma range left after box-filtering to 64 and 24 px. Built for icons/drawings; mnemo withdrew a finding that misread it as text legibility.

measurement.formula: retained = min(1, range_small/range_full); survives if >= 0.6

axes.validation: explicit caveat (T8 withdrawn)
axes.scifin_reason: Not a screen-legibility measure; only useful for an app icon.
axes.port_inputs: PNG

axes.name: Typeface voice fit (model-judged)
axes.definition: An LLM judges whether the font pairing carries the brand voice; contrast, separation and rhythm are excluded because they are computed.

measurement.formula: LLM 0..1; others scaled by 0.78

axes.scifin_reason: Typeface choice is a one-time decision for Sci-Fin, not a per-screen variant axis.
axes.port_inputs: n/a

axes.name: Primary-action spacing
axes.definition: Smallest gap between the submit target and any other target, keyboard top included (more is safer).

measurement.formula: min distance between submit box and other boxes

axes.validation: Model layouts re-rendered and re-measured (tier_t1).
axes.scifin_reason: Save button next to the numeric keypad on the Add sheet.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON bounds incl. keyboard/keypad

axes.name: Data line / stroke at least 1 dp
axes.definition: Strokes defined in px dissolve on high-density screens; goal lines/bars need >= 1 dp (Material minimum).

measurement.inputs: source (px literals in Canvas draws) or rendered PNG ink runs at known density
measurement.formula: dp = px / (dpi/160); icon_check: Nth-percentile horizontal ink run -> dp at render size; ok >= 2 dp, warn >= 1.2, block < 1.2

axes.scifin_reason: Budget progress and goal lines in Sci-Fin charts.
axes.port_inputs: PNG at known density + chart rects, or Canvas source

axes.name: Overflow, cut-off and clipped-text defects
axes.definition: Defect counts (not scores): body content taller than its viewport (controls below the fold), widgets horizontally cut off, and text whose minimum size hint exceeds its box. Long paths must be middle-elided with the full text in a tooltip.

measurement.inputs: widget dump (rect vs visible rect, minimumSizeHint, scroll area content vs viewport)
measurement.formula: overflow_px = max(0, content_h - viewport_h); cut = vis.w < rect.w - 1 and not scrolling; clipped = hint.w > w + 1 (or height for wrapped)

axes.aggregation: Listed in defects.md with screenshot path; not in overall.
axes.validation: Found 3 overflows and 2 squashed inputs; test asserts elided label keeps full text in tooltip.
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Critical for money: a clipped or elided amount is a correctness bug; Sci-Fin should forbid elision on amount nodes and flag any text whose intrinsic width exceeds its box at 360dp and with large font scale.
axes.port_inputs: probe nodes with measured vs intrinsic width, scroll container content/viewport heights
axes.fit_reason: Critical for money: a clipped or elided amount is a correctness bug; Sci-Fin should forbid elision on amount nodes and flag any text whose intrinsic width exceeds its box at 360dp and with large font scale.

axes.name: Predictable (items move on their own)
axes.definition: 1 when the order changes on its own as use changes (most-recent-first, hybrid fits), 0 when it is manual; plus log_varies/unconfirmed (what Log does varies per row).

measurement.formula: moves = 1 if order in (recent, hybrid) else 0

axes.scifin_reason: Category picker sorted by recent use vs fixed order.
axes.port_inputs: declared

axes.name: Prerequisite control first
axes.definition: A control that depends on another being set (Folder before Schedule before Back up now; Require unlock before Lock grace) comes after it.

measurement.formula: per page fraction of present (a,b) pairs with pos[a] < pos[b]; mean over pages

axes.scifin_reason: Sci-Fin settings: base currency before display format, backup folder before schedule, PIN before lock timeout.
axes.port_inputs: row order + precedence pairs

axes.name: Spacing grid adherence and sprawl
axes.definition: Share of padding, margin and gap values that are multiples of the grid unit, and the number of distinct spacing values.

measurement.formula: off = values where |v/grid - round(v/grid)| > 0.01; note if off non-empty and more than 2 values; warn if >10 distinct values.

axes.scifin_reason: Probe bbox gaps and paddings in dp against a 4dp/8dp grid. Convert from px using the known density before testing.
axes.port_inputs: Probe element insets and inter-element gaps in dp

axes.name: Spacing on the 4/8 dp grid and via tokens
axes.source: mnemo_pass4/mnemo/tools/design_critique_2026_09_18/measure_layout.py:89-113; GlassCam_fixed/GlassCam/tools/critique/measure.py:171,279-287; chronicle docs/critique-2026-09-15.md:170-178 (276 raw .dp literals vs ChronicleDimens)
axes.definition: Spacing values fall on a 4 dp (ideally 8 dp) rhythm and come from dimension tokens rather than raw literals; an off-rhythm tail (6, 10, 18, 22 dp) is what tokens would not have produced.

measurement.inputs: static: Kotlin/XML dp literal census; rendered: gaps between sibling rects in probe JSON
measurement.formula: share_on4 = count(v % 4 == 0)/total; share_on8 likewise; token adoption = token uses / (token uses + raw literals)

axes.validation: regex counts are upper bounds; chronicle histogram showed the token values were the five most used
axes.scifin_reason: Probe JSON gives actual inter-element gaps at known density, better than a source census.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON sibling rects (or source scan)
sources: mnemo_pass4/mnemo/tools/design_critique_2026_09_18/measure_layout.py:89-113; GlassCam_fixed/GlassCam/tools/critique/measure.py:171,279-287; chronicle docs/critique-2026-09-15.md:170-178 (276 raw .dp literals vs ChronicleDimens)

axes.name: Vertical spacing rhythm (1a, harmony half)
axes.definition: Whether vertical gaps between stacked elements sit on the 4 px grid and use few distinct values (a named spacing ramp), i.e. a calm rhythm. Polish version scored only share of gaps off the 4 px grid (lower better).

measurement.formula: for each leaf, gap to nearest leaf below that overlaps horizontally; keep 0 < g <= GUTTER_MAX; on_grid = share(g % 4 == 0); distinct = |set(gaps)|; harmony = 100*on_grid*min(1, FLUENT_GAPS/distinct)

axes.validation: none beyond the run
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Compose uses a 4/8dp spacing scale; the gap-on-grid and distinct-gap count apply unchanged to probe rects in dp.
axes.port_inputs: leaf rects in dp; Sci-Fin's spacing ramp size (number of named spacing tokens) for FLUENT_GAPS
axes.fit_reason: Compose uses a 4/8dp spacing scale; the gap-on-grid and distinct-gap count apply unchanged to probe rects in dp.

axes.name: Space between adjacent targets (1g, part)
axes.definition: Share of neighbouring target pairs separated by at least the minimum visible gap, so adjacent buttons are not mis-hit.

measurement.formula: pairs = clickable pairs overlapping on one axis with gap < ADJACENT; tight = pairs with gap < TARGET_GAP; part = 100*(1 - tight/pairs)

axes.validation: test_layout_rules.py:102 asserts >= 32+4 px between header/footer position buttons.
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Category chips and keypad-like entry rows on phone need this; use 8dp gap.
axes.port_inputs: clickable rects in dp
axes.fit_reason: Category chips and keypad-like entry rows on phone need this; use 8dp gap.

axes.name: Toast notice: look distance, undo seen, read margin
axes.definition: How far a toast sits from where the person acted (px), whether Undo is seen, and the safety margin: toast duration minus time to read its longest text at 238 wpm.

measurement.inputs: DOM: toast and acting element positions; toast text
measurement.formula: look = mean |undo.y - act.y| (desktop: hypot); read_s = words / (238/60); margin_s = timing - read_s(longest)

axes.scifin_reason: 'Transaction added / deleted, Undo' snackbar placement relative to Add and tab bar.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON of snackbar and acted-on element; snackbar text and duration

axes.name: Density vs a reference page (1a, density half)
axes.definition: How close a screen's whitespace share and control count per area sit to a modelled reference page (a Fluent settings page built from spec tokens), so screens are neither cramped nor empty. Evolved from _polish-2026-10-08/score.py 'density' = median share of content area covered by controls (raw, higher = denser, no target).

measurement.inputs: widget geometry dump (visible clipped rects of leaf widgets, page rect, clickable flags)
measurement.formula: ws = 1 - union_area(leaf rects)/area(page) (coordinate-compression union); cpa = clickables/(area(page)/1e5); density = mean(100*max(0,1-|ws-WS_REF|/WS_REF), 100*max(0,1-|log2(cpa/CPA_REF)|/2))

constants.WS_REF: computed from a 1000-wide settings row model: row 68, gap 4, pad 16, control 120x32, text block 36 tall, header-control gap 24

axes.aggregation: Averaged 50/50 with spacing_harmony into axis 1a; 1a is one of ten equally weighted axes in 'overall' (mean). Placement variants compared by mean, TIE = 0.5 point.
axes.validation: Run on 26 screens x 2 placements x 2 window sizes; group A scored ~80, collections ~20 (scores.md).
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Useful for phone 360dp vs desktop, but the reference model must be rebuilt from Material 3 list-item/card tokens rather than Fluent settings rows.
axes.port_inputs: layout probe JSON with leaf node rects + clickable flag + content-area rect, at known density (dp)
axes.fit_reason: Useful for phone 360dp vs desktop, but the reference model must be rebuilt from Material 3 list-item/card tokens rather than Fluent settings rows.

measurement.formula: 1 - inversions / (n(n-1)/2)

axes.name: Detail distribution (edge-energy Gini)
axes.definition: Gini coefficient of edge energy over a 12x12 grid. Uniform detail gives the eye nowhere to land; extreme clumping leaves dead space.

measurement.formula: gini over cell sums; uniform if gini < 0.35; clumped if gini > 0.8 and empty_share > 0.6 (empty = cell < total/(n*20))

axes.scifin_reason: A usable proxy for visual density and hierarchy on dense finance screens; calibrate bands on existing Sci-Fin renders.
axes.port_inputs: PNG

axes.name: Detail spread (edge Gini, empty share)
axes.definition: How unevenly detail (Sobel edge energy) is spread across a 12x12 grid; a proxy for clutter vs focus and for empty regions.

measurement.formula: cells = sum of Sobel magnitude per 12x12 cell; gini = 2*sum((i+1)v_i)/(n*total) - (n+1)/n; empty_share = share of cells with energy < total/(20n); uniform if gini < 0.35, clumped if > 0.8

axes.scifin_reason: Dashboard density comparison phone vs desktop and vs references; no absolute target.
axes.port_inputs: PNG renders

axes.name: Rendered value (tonal) structure
axes.definition: Luminance distribution of a screenshot: p5-p95 range, how many of 5 value bands hold >= 2% of pixels, dominant band share. Read relative to reference apps shot on the same phone ('apples to apples').

measurement.inputs: PNG cropped to app area (rows 100-2280 of 1080x2412)
measurement.formula: range = p95 - p5 of luma; bands_occupied = count(share_b >= 0.02) over 5 bands; flat if range < 0.15; has_structure if >= 3 bands and max share < 0.8

axes.validation: mnemo T8 withdrawn: a craftkit number was misread as text legibility. These are composition metrics built for drawings, not UI verdicts.
axes.scifin_reason: Comparative only (Sci-Fin dark vs light, vs reference finance apps); dark UI screens naturally score 'flat'.
axes.port_inputs: Sci-Fin PNG renders (crop system bars)

axes.name: Behaviour-case coverage per owner vs schema growth
axes.definition: Model contests: share of each owner's behaviour cases an option expresses (0/0.5/1, simulated results override hand marks) against schema growth (tables + columns + enum cases); options with violations rejected; a control must fail its expected cases or the run exits 2.

measurement.formula: cov[owner] = mean(expresses); growth = tables+columns+enum_cases; Pareto (cov high, growth low)

axes.validation: Control gate: exit 2 if the control passes a case it must fail.
axes.scifin_reason: Schema/data-model contest, not a screen axis; the control-gate idea transfers (see notes).

axes.name: Narrative flow (model-judged)
axes.definition: An LLM reads the section order as a reader meets it and judges whether each section lands with the context the previous ones built.

measurement.formula: LLM score 0..1; base components scaled by 0.75 to make room

axes.scifin_reason: Built for argument-style documents; app screens are scanned, not read as a narrative.
axes.port_inputs: n/a

axes.name: Clutter (edge density)
axes.definition: Share of pixels that sit on an edge in the rendered screen; a proxy for visual clutter (nav_glance cites Mack & Oliva 2004). The owner's complaint was options that are 'difficult to parse at a glance'.

measurement.inputs: PNG render (headless Edge, 360x740 phone, 1100x660 desktop), light and dark
measurement.formula: grey = PIL convert('L'); edges = ImageFilter.FIND_EDGES; clutter = count(edge px >= 40/255) / (w*h); mean over light+dark. User-data dotted outlines are hidden before measuring (.score .ud{outline:none}).
measurement.range: 0..1; Factotum screens 0.018-0.057; reference apps 0.011 (Loop) .. 0.079 (Anytype), scaled to 360 px wide

axes.aggregation: Objective in every Pareto front (phone 'clutter' and 'desk_clutter' separately); differences < 0.002 treated as ties. In toast/t2/t3 parts it sits in a 'Calm' axis summed by ranks.
axes.validation: Threshold robustness checked in nav-glance.md at 20/40/80/120: depth coding beat plain and hue in 48/48 at every threshold. reference_clutter() measures real apps' screenshots for calibration. Controls (busy header 0.034 vs 0.033; dense rows 0.057 vs 0.036-0.040) lose.
axes.scifin_reason: Pure pixel metric; works on any Sci-Fin PNG at known density once scaled to 360 dp wide.
axes.port_inputs: PNG per screen per theme, plus a dp scale factor to normalise to 360 dp width; optional mask for user data

axes.name: Motivational register fit
axes.definition: Whether a screen's layout pattern, primary emphasis and sections carry the motivational tone (0 ambient .. 1 urgent) and comparison referent the screen's purpose calls for. Stops a recurring-use tracker from reading as an alarm panel (or hiding what must be acted on).

measurement.formula: pattern_score = 1 if tone inside pattern's tone band else max(0, 1 - off/0.30); untoned inherited patterns = 0.70. emphasis: urgent-word match -> tone; ambient-word match -> 1-tone; neither/both -> 1-|tone-0.5|. coherent = 1, set 0.15 if status-board+ambient emphasis or ambient-reflection+urgent emphasis; min(coherent,0.35) if referent social-peer without peer section or none/self-history with peer section (leaderboard/friends/peer/ranking/community). If 0.40<=tone<=0.60 and one-sided emphasis: emphasis=min(emphasis,0.75). register_fit = 0.40*pattern + 0.30*emphasis + 0.30*coherent.

axes.weighting: 0.20 of app-register fitness (register.py:91 WEIGHTS_WITH_REGISTER); dropped for registerless screens (--exempt).
axes.scifin_reason: Built for recurring-use finance/habit trackers; anchors put a personal budget tracker at tone 0.75/fixed-target and an investment tracker at 0.45/self-history.
axes.port_inputs: Per screen (or zone): pattern label, primary-emphasis section id, ordered section ids taken from the JSON layout probe; target tone and referent declared per screen in a Sci-Fin register table.

axes.name: Rows in view (density)
axes.definition: Item rows wholly inside the phone's content area: 'how much of the day fits at a glance'.

measurement.inputs: DOM: .body .row bounds vs .body bounds (later: above the bar's top)
measurement.formula: count(row.top >= body.top and row.bottom <= body.bottom)

axes.aggregation: 'Density' axis (-rows_seen) in t2/t3 rank sums, together with cut titles.
axes.scifin_reason: Transactions per screen above the tab bar on 360 dp.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON: list row bounds, content viewport bounds (above tab bar)

axes.name: Visual mass and emphasis coherence
axes.source: tools/screens/sheet_weight.py:45-56; capture_v2.py:153-176, 196-205; hub_opt.py:141; picker_opt.py:183 (heavy); t2_opt.py:1055 (mass, dismiss_pull)
axes.definition: Mass = summed departure of each pixel's luminance from the region's ground tone, per element box; checks that the content outweighs the button that submits it and that the two heaviest elements follow the declared importance order. Owner: a big black check 'creates a huge imbalance between the elements on the sheet'.

measurement.formula: ground = modal luma bin (32 bins); mass(box) = sum |luma - ground|; add_share = mass(add)/mass(sheet); add_vs_line = mass(add)/mass(line) (<= 1); heavy = max element share; headers share; dismiss_pull = m_dismiss/(m_dismiss+m_snooze); emphasis = designkit layout.emphasis_coherence(top2 by mass, importance order)

axes.aggregation: Harmony axis (rank sum) in capture_v2/v3/v4, hub_opt, picker, repeat3; 'Half-asleep' axis in alarm.
axes.validation: Added because the reach-only search could not see the imbalance (sheet_weight docstring).
axes.scifin_reason: Does the balance figure outweigh the Add button and the chart; is Delete heavier than Save.
axes.port_inputs: PNG at known density + probe JSON bounds with roles and a declared importance order
sources: tools/screens/sheet_weight.py:45-56; capture_v2.py:153-176, 196-205; hub_opt.py:141; picker_opt.py:183 (heavy); t2_opt.py:1055 (mass, dismiss_pull)

axes.name: Cognitive load (density and depth calibration)
axes.definition: Density against the audience's band and hierarchy depth against content volume, plus the joint rule that dense content needs navigation depth.

measurement.formula: d_score = 1 in band else max(0, 1-off/0.30); h_score = 1 in band else max(0, 1-off/2); joint = 0.4 if density>0.7 and depth<3, 0.6 if density<0.3 and depth>3, else 1. load = 0.45*d + 0.35*h + 0.20*joint.

axes.scifin_reason: Density has to be measured rather than chosen, for example text and ink area over the viewport from the probe or PNG; depth comes from distinct heading levels.
axes.port_inputs: Probe: element/text area coverage per viewport (or imgstat ink_coverage), count of distinct heading levels; audience = general, volume per screen.

axes.name: Emphasis coherence
axes.definition: Whether primary and secondary emphasis fall on the most important sections, or, with no declared importance, on early load-bearing ones.

measurement.formula: Primary == secondary -> 0. With ranking: +0.6 if primary==rank[0] (0.35 if in top 2); +0.4 if secondary==rank[1] (0.2 if in top 3). Without ranking: 0.6*(1-pos(primary)/(n-1)) + 0.4*(1-|pos(secondary)-1|/(n-1)). Capped at 1.

axes.scifin_reason: Needs 'which section is emphasised' derived from the render, for example the largest type, highest contrast or most area per section in the probe.
axes.port_inputs: Per-section salience from the probe (max font size, bbox area, filled/accent background) to rank primary and secondary; declared importance list.

axes.name: Focal point and left/right balance
axes.definition: Where edge energy concentrates (and whether it lands on the content or on the action), and the share of mass left of centre.

measurement.formula: imgstat._focal_report (edge-energy centroid) mapped to element box; balance = mass_left/mass_total

axes.aggregation: Reported in sheet_weight.json; not a ranked axis elsewhere.
axes.scifin_reason: Focal on the money figure is the check Sci-Fin wants; needs edge-energy centroid code.
axes.port_inputs: PNG + probe bounds with role

axes.name: Glanceable value vs bystander exposure
axes.definition: A launcher tile trades how much of the answer it gives without opening (glance) against what a bystander learns (exposure) and whether it can be stale (freshness).

measurement.inputs: static design vector (lock policy, wording, content, refresh, sizes, theme)
measurement.formula: exposure = min(1, (LOCK + WORDING)/2 + ENABLE); glance = CONTENT * WORDING * SIZES; freshness = lookup; fit = (THEME + CONTENT)/2; effort = 1 - normalised points

axes.validation: lookup tables are judgement; docstring cites sources where they exist
axes.scifin_reason: Money figures are sensitive: balance visibility on widgets, notifications, recents thumbnail and a 'hide amounts' mode is the same exposure-vs-glance trade.
axes.port_inputs: design options table for amount visibility

axes.name: Layout constraints (emphasis distinct, depth cap, dense-needs-nav)
axes.definition: Three feasibility rules: primary emphasis is not secondary emphasis; hierarchy depth is at most the medium's cap; density above 0.7 requires depth of at least 3.

measurement.formula: Each returns 1/0 (scorers.py:142,146,151)

axes.scifin_reason: The dashboard depth cap of 2 and the dense-needs-depth-3 rule conflict for a dense phone dashboard. Recalibrate them for app screens.
axes.port_inputs: Same probe-derived density and depth.

axes.name: Rendered focal point vs composition anchors
axes.definition: Centroid of Sobel edge energy, and its distance to centre, thirds or golden anchors. A proxy for where the eye lands.

measurement.formula: centroid = edge-weighted mean (x,y)/size; nearest anchor of centre(0.5,0.5), thirds(1/3), golden(0.618) and mirrors; on_anchor if d <= 0.06; unplaced if d > 0.12

axes.scifin_reason: For screens, compare the centroid with the bbox of the declared primary-emphasis section instead of art anchors. That gives a computed emphasis check for emphasis_coherence and register.
axes.port_inputs: PNG plus primary section bbox from the probe

axes.source: tools/screens/t3_opt.py:2244-2268 (like_today, like_when, like_item_page); toast_opt AXES g (spread_px, ways_in); actions_opt (sort_stray, duplicate_paths, one_model)

axes.name: Actions over a task set (walked)

measurement.formula: ID = log2(hypot(rest - centre) / min(w, h) + 1); reach = mean over targets

axes.definition: Counted risks: edits lost on back without asking, an accidental destructive action reachable by a common gesture, a multi-selection silently applying to a subset, gesture clashes with scroll, the distance between the 'go' and 'keep' buttons, an extra confirming step.

axes.definition: Share of clickable controls meeting the minimum target size; a switch's target is its whole box, not the drawn pill. axes.name: Touch-target floor (48 dp)
axes.source: GlassCam_fixed/GlassCam/tools/critique/scorers.py:105; GlassCam_fixed/GlassCam/tools/critique/settings_compare.py:76 (uiautomator); GlassCam_fixed/GlassCam/tools/critique/measure.py:184 (layout XML); mnemo_pass4/mnemo/tools/design_critique_2026_09_18/measure_layout.py:98 (regex); chronicle-native/tools/layout_lint.py:329 (small-touch-target); Personal assistant project/design/selection/scorers.py:89 (neighbour-risk variant)
axes.definition: Every tappable element is at least 48 dp in both dimensions; smaller targets invite the neighbour. GlassCam: 'Touch-target compliance: every cell is column_dp square; 48 dp is the floor.'

measurement.inputs: uiautomator dump (bounds of clickable/checkable nodes, px -> dp via density) or layout probe JSON; static fallbacks: layout XML / Kotlin regex for size literals within one line of a click token
measurement.formula: per target: s = min(1, min(w_dp,h_dp)/48)^2 (GlassCam optimiser). Census form: count(min(w,h) < 48), median_h_dp, min_h_dp over clickable nodes (settings_compare). PA variant for dense grids: accuracy = 1 - max(0,(48 - w)/48) (x0.6 for drag pads)

constants.PA_SCREEN: 360 dp wide, 24 dp margins -> 312 dp control

measurement.direction: higher score / fewer under-48 is better

axes.weighting: GlassCam shutter layout 0.15 of 5 components; PA accuracy 0.30 of 3. Census forms are gates/reports, not weighted.
axes.validation: settings_compare docstring warns nodes are TAPPABLES not rows (search field + chips counted); pages with <5 titled top-level tappables are reported 'not exposed to accessibility' instead of scored. mnemo notes regex is an upper bound and misses unsized controls (bare Switch). layout_lint has a --self-test fixture set.
axes.scifin_reason: Tab bar, Add/entry button, budget rows and settings switches all need >=48 dp at 360 dp phone; probe JSON already carries rects.
axes.port_inputs: layout probe JSON rects of clickable nodes + density

axes.definition: The judged half of the nine critique dimensions: 2-second first impression and emotional register; a single clear entry point and reading order; whitespace doing structural work; fit for channel and audience; whether the signature element lands.

measurement.formula: Located findings with severity High (blocks usability or legibility, fails WCAG, wrong first impression), Med (weakens effectiveness, inconsistency visible to non-designers), Low (polish). Measured and judged findings are kept in separate voices.

constants.judgement_dims: first impression, visual hierarchy, fit for purpose, copy voice, originality, signature element (uilint.py:421)

measurement.formula: s_find = 0.5*min(1, cue_px2/max cue_px2) + 0.5*current_visible_everywhere

axes.validation: none

axes.name: Mis-tap risk under scatter
axes.definition: A tap aimed at the safe target's centre lands with a round Gaussian scatter; aim_risk = probability it lands on a destructive target, snooze_miss = probability it misses the intended one, slap_risk = share of screen that acts on a blind tap. Added because without it a control reached the front.

measurement.inputs: DOM boxes of intended and dangerous targets
measurement.formula: P_in(box) = Phi_x * Phi_y with sigma; aim = sum over bad boxes P_in; miss = 1 - P_in(intended); slap = sum(bad area)/(360*740)

measurement.formula: picks summed; s_effort = 1 - picks/worst picks

axes.aggregation: Mean of effort, safety, predictability, calm.
axes.validation: Inventory of real behaviour measured first (memory-inventory.md, probe_memory.py).

measurement.formula: 20 resize steps 1000x700 -> 1920x1000; change = CPU share over 1 s after open_tool; idle = CPU share over 10 s; score = mean(100*min(1, target/value)) over resize_worst_ms, change_cpu_pct, idle_cpu_pct; differences under one clock tick are ties

axes.definition: Per app: entry-point position (dp from bottom-right), taps to reach settings, rows shown on the first settings screen, search present - compared across reference apps.

measurement.inputs: uiautomator dump of entry screen and settings screen
measurement.formula: taps count; entry distance dp; rows_first_screen = top-level tappables; search = any EditText or content-desc starting search

axes.name: Modelled completion time (Hick + Fitts)
axes.definition: Time to complete a one-tap entry: Hick-Hyman decision time plus Fitts pointing (plus drag settle / confirm tap), against a 10 s daily-touch budget.

measurement.inputs: static model of the control (number of choices, target width, travel distance, drag vs tap, confirm step)
measurement.formula: T = 0.150*log2(states+1) + (0.10 + 0.15*log2(d/w + 1)) [+0.4 drag] [+0.6 confirm]; sliders: two decisions and two drags; speed = clamp(1 - (T-1)/9, 0, 1)

axes.weighting: speed 0.4, resolution 0.3 (1 - exp(-states/12)), accuracy 0.3; Pareto front (front_capacity 16), described by the owner as 'explorative - a front of defensible shapes, not a verdict'.
axes.validation: none beyond published typical constants
axes.scifin_reason: Score quick-entry flows (category grid vs list, amount keypad, confirm step) for the Add-expense path; the 'resolution' term is check-in specific and does not carry.

measurement.formula: share = content.w*content.h/(window.w*window.h)

axes.validation: Compared CustomTkinter vs PySide6 prototypes.

axes.name: Register guard (no urgency, grading or guilt)
axes.source: Personal assistant project/design/copy/score.py:46; chronicle docs/chronicle-design-audit.md section 3 (motivational_tone ~0.3)
axes.definition: Penalise banned urgency/grading/system-talk words, exclamation marks and a second sentence on daily screens (settings/widget exempt).

measurement.formula: 1 - (0.5*|words in BANNED| + 0.5*[has '!'] + 0.5*[>1 sentence and not exempt]), clamped >= 0

axes.scifin_reason: Over-budget and missed-goal copy in a finance app is exactly where shaming words creep in; banned list needs a finance edit (overspent, behind, failed).

axes.name: Copy tone: words, reading grade, cheer, blame
axes.definition: For every sentence a state shows: word count, Flesch-Kincaid grade, cheer (congratulating words, '!', emoji) and blame (words putting fault on the user). Rule: 'one plain sentence and one action, no illustration, no cheer, no guilt'.

measurement.inputs: Static strings drawn on the screen
measurement.formula: grade = 0.39*words/sentences + 11.8*syllables/words - 15.59 (syllables = vowel groups, minus silent final e); cheer = count(CHEER words) + '!' + pictographic emoji; blame = count(BLAME phrases)

axes.validation: Word lists are a stated assumption from the 2026-10-07 rule, not a study. Compared with 16 phone apps (empty-references.json).
axes.scifin_reason: Empty ledger, over-budget and error copy in a money app is exactly where blame/cheer creep in.
axes.port_inputs: string resources per screen state

axes.name: Purpose-driven tone and referent placement
axes.definition: Name why the user opens the screen, then place motivational_tone and comparison_referent against worked anchors. Purpose beats category: debt payoff under distress sits lower than a routine budget tracker.

measurement.formula: Model reasons from the two nearest anchors (nearest_anchors(tone, k=2), register.py:97) and states a one-sentence reason. The anchors are a reference, not a formula.
measurement.direction: n/a (sets the target that register_fit scores against)

axes.name: Screen memory: interruptions
axes.definition: Number of questions (save/discard prompts) a policy asks over the scenarios.

measurement.formula: s_calm = 1 - prompts/worst prompts

axes.validation: as above
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Discard-draft dialogs on the entry sheet.
axes.port_inputs: policy + scenarios
axes.fit_reason: Discard-draft dialogs on the entry sheet.

axes.name: Visual balance and ink coverage
axes.definition: Mass (departure from the dominant ground tone) split left/right and top/bottom, and the share of pixels that are not ground.

measurement.formula: ground = modal luma bin of 32; w = |luma-ground|; horizontal = left mass share; vertical = top share; ink = share(w > 0.04); lopsided if |h-0.5| > 0.28; blank if ink < 0.03

axes.scifin_reason: ink_coverage is a ready computed density input for cognitive_load; left/right balance matters more on the desktop layout.
axes.port_inputs: PNG

axes.name: Visual mass balance and ink coverage
axes.definition: Mass = departure from the most common tone; share of mass in the left half and top half, and fraction of non-ground pixels.

measurement.formula: ground = modal luma bin of 32; w = |luma - ground|; horizontal = sum_left w / sum w; vertical = sum_top w / sum w; ink = share(w > 0.04); centred if both within 0.08 of 0.5

axes.scifin_reason: Detect top-heavy hero cards or empty lower halves on 360 dp phone; comparative.
axes.port_inputs: PNG renders

axes.name: Cross-zone visual coherence (multi-module screen)
axes.definition: When one screen combines zones from modules with different tones, the high-tone zone must not dominate just because red reads louder than beige (Trigger B). A triggered zone is allowed to dominate.

measurement.formula: Rubric only. Each zone keeps its native tone (no averaging); check shared type scale, consistent spacing and deliberate visual weighting across zones (register-calibration.md:164,194).

axes.scifin_reason: The Sci-Fin home/overview probably mixes a budget zone (about 0.75) with an investment or savings zone (about 0.45). This can be made computable from per-zone saliency in the PNG (for example imgstat edge energy or chroma per zone bbox).
axes.port_inputs: Zone bounding boxes from the layout probe, PNG crop per zone, per-zone tone.

axes.name: Body leading ratio
axes.definition: Body line-height / size >= 1.4 (design-critique-plus floor), headings tighter; scored with designkit line_height_score.

measurement.formula: lh/size; designkit line_height_score(ratio)

axes.scifin_reason: Static check of Sci-Fin Typography.

axes.name: Context kept (rows still visible behind)
axes.source: tools/screens/t2_opt.py AXES 'page' Context (-context_rows); t3_opt addsent/addhabit; toast_opt line_covered (screen_score.py:81)
axes.definition: Rows of the list still visible while an item page/sheet is open; line_covered: whether the typed capture line is hidden by something above it (sampled at 10/50/90% of its width).

measurement.formula: context_rows = count(list rows seen with overlay open); line_covered = any(elementFromPoint(x_f, y_mid) not in line, f in {0.1,0.5,0.9})

axes.aggregation: Context axis; line_covered in Cover axis.
axes.scifin_reason: Seeing the ledger or budget while entering an expense.

axes.name: Open/Add placement: vertical space taken
axes.definition: Vertical pixels the entry area consumes in the page body (and, on prototypes, px from the title's top to the first options card), i.e. how far the screen's own content is pushed down.

measurement.formula: s_compact = max(0, 1 - mean(file_area_px)/today); prototypes: mean(first card top - title top)

axes.validation: Prototype: 118 px (nav) vs 173 px today.
axes.scifin_fit_reason: On a 360dp phone, how far an inline entry bar pushes the balance/budget content down is a first-order cost.

axes.name: Finance numerals: tabular figures, right-aligned, decimals aligned
axes.definition: Stacked amounts use tabular figures, are right-aligned, and have the decimal point aligned down the column; dates use an unambiguous format.

measurement.formula: Not coded in the skill. Computable: per column, spread of right edges (or decimal-separator x) is at most 1 dp; tnum enabled; dates not bare numeric.

axes.scifin_reason: Transaction lists and budget tables are Sci-Fin's main surfaces; probe bboxes make this a cheap computed check.
axes.port_inputs: Probe amount nodes (bbox right edge, text) grouped by list; decimal glyph x by width measurement or tnum assumption

axes.name: Frequency-weighted taps including scrolls (or search)
axes.definition: Every item's typical use weighted by how often it happens, plus the scrolls needed to bring its control into view, or a search when cheaper; scored at two list sizes and the worse rank counts. Owner: taller cards 'increase the amount of scrolling ... and hide a lot of trackers'.

measurement.inputs: DOM bounds of each item's control, viewport bottom (bar top), list page height; usage frequency profile
measurement.formula: scrolls = 0 if bottom <= vb else ceil((bottom - vb)/page); reach_cost = min(scrolls + fold_tap, SEARCH_COST); cost = sum f*(entry_taps + visits*reach_cost)/sum f

axes.aggregation: max-of-ranks across sizes ('max:' keys); leads the front.
axes.validation: Replaced T3b.1b because scroll was undercounted (owner, 2026-10-13).
axes.scifin_reason: Category/account pickers and budget lists at small and large counts; frequency profile from spending categories.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON of list at N=12 and N=40, viewport/tab-bar bounds, per-item frequency table

axes.name: Everyday rows first
axes.definition: Rows touched often sit high on the page: the frequency-weighted position sum normalised between the best and worst possible orders.

measurement.inputs: ordered rows per page + frequency class per row
measurement.formula: w_i = FREQ[row_i]; actual = sum(i*w_i); best = same with w sorted desc; worst = sorted asc; score = 1 - (actual-best)/(worst-best); pages with <2 distinct weights skipped; mean over pages

axes.weighting: 0.35 of 4 (largest); shipped 0.77 because risk_last conflicts on the hub.
axes.validation: README notes the measured trade-off (Backup cannot be both rare and below midpoint with Security last).
axes.scifin_reason: Settings hub and tab order (Overview/Transactions/Budgets/Goals) ordered by use frequency.
axes.port_inputs: row/tab order + a frequency table

axes.name: Smallest text
axes.definition: The smallest font size of any visible text node, in px; T1 scores the shortfall below a 14 px floor.

measurement.inputs: DOM text nodes with non-zero box, computed font-size
measurement.formula: min_text = min(fontSize); min_text_short = max(0, 14 - min_text); capture line text_small = 18 - font

axes.aggregation: min_text_short in T1 Pareto low-set; '-min_text' in Legibility axes.
axes.scifin_reason: Probe can report sp per text; scale-aware.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON: text nodes with font size in sp/dp

axes.name: Named in 1 (screens named on persistent nav)
axes.definition: Screens whose own name is always on screen; a module label like 'Routines' names no single screen. Owner: 'pick a feature by its name'.

measurement.formula: len(named1)

axes.scifin_reason: Tab labels 'Budgets', 'Goals' vs a vague 'Plan'.
axes.port_inputs: static nav definition

axes.name: Weekly navigation cost
axes.definition: Sum over every sought screen of its weekly weight x steps, with half a step added when the route works only from one place; screens have a home area and a depth, candidates state area costs and hubs (drawer, ⊞ sheet, top row, pin).

measurement.inputs: Static model: screens (weight, area, depth), candidate area costs and hub listings
measurement.formula: steps = min(area_cost + depth, hub_cost + 1); exp = steps + (0 if anywhere else 0.5); cost = sum w*exp; search-only areas cost search+1

axes.aggregation: Pareto with tail, max_depth, visible, hub, start_load, switch (low) and register, reach2, named1 (high); A++ pins chosen by enumerating all 3-pin combinations by cost.
axes.validation: nav_home.py reports how results move with NOT_ANYWHERE; reference apps measured by taps-per-job protocol (reference-protocol.md) for comparison.
axes.scifin_reason: Tab bar slots vs Add, budgets, goals, accounts, reports weighted by how often each is used.
axes.port_inputs: static screen list with weekly weights, area/depth, and each nav candidate's routes

axes.name: Overview (items in view) and screens spanned
axes.definition: Share of items in view or behind a label header in view (one tap), and how many screens the list spans.

measurement.inputs: DOM bounds of items/headers vs viewport
measurement.formula: overview = in_view/N; screens = ceil(list_height / page)

axes.aggregation: Overview axis, max of ranks over 12/30/40 items.
axes.scifin_reason: How many budgets/categories/accounts are visible without scrolling.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON at multiple list sizes

axes.name: Main action outweighs other controls (1f, second half)
axes.source: _qt-2026-10-09/phase6/after/measure.py:820 (ax_hierarchy) and pixel visual weight :438; polish 'exactly one primary' _polish-2026-10-08/score.py:377,409
axes.definition: Share of other text controls that the primary action visually outweighs, where visual weight is measured from screenshot pixels. Polish version: count screens without exactly one accent-filled bold button >= 120 px wide.

measurement.formula: ground g = modal grey on a 1 px ring 2 px outside the control; visual_weight = w*h*mean(|grey - g|)/255; dom = 100*(1 - #others with weight >= primary / #others)

axes.validation: none beyond the run

axes.name: Purpose-integrity gate (engagement-serving framing)
axes.definition: A hard gate: does softening or sharpening the register serve the user's own goal, or engagement, spend or attention? If it serves engagement, stop and flag. Never a weighted component.

measurement.formula: Binary pass/flag answered by reasoning. Partial credit is explicitly disallowed.

axes.scifin_reason: A finance app is the textbook case: debt and spend screens can be softened for wellbeing or to drive engagement.

axes.name: No overflow/clip at raised font scale or 360 dp
axes.source: chronicle-native-pending/chronicle-native/tools/layout_lint.py:269-344 (rules row-overflow, unscrollable-action, fixed-height-text, small-touch-target, maxlines-no-overflow); chronicle docs/walk-2026-09-16.md:47 (W4/W13 status line wraps at 360 dp); mnemo design_critique_2026_09_18/critique.md:61 (plain Row text beside a control cut at rest)
axes.definition: Controls must not leave the viewport and labels must not clip or wrap unexpectedly at font scale 1.3x/2.0x or at 360 dp width; Mimirae shipped two such losses ('the control was simply gone').

measurement.inputs: static Compose source shapes (lint) or, better, probe JSON at fontScale 1.0/1.3/2.0: text line counts, ellipsis flags, node rect vs parent/viewport
measurement.formula: lint: count of findings per rule. Rendered form: count(nodes with rect outside viewport or parent) + count(single-line labels with lineCount>1) + count(clipped text without ellipsis); 0 = pass

axes.weighting: report, not gate (exit 0); chronicle's 10 row-overflow advisories were left 'unknown, not fixed' pending device checks
axes.validation: --self-test against tools/layout_fixtures (positive and negative fixtures); the lint was found broken twice (trailing lambdas, clickable Surfaces) before the self-test existed. uiautomator misses glyph Text inside clickable Box (two false findings withdrawn).
axes.scifin_reason: Money figures and budget labels at 360 dp and large font scale are the classic overflow risk; Sci-Fin probes at known density can measure it directly.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON at multiple fontScales: text rects, lineCount, hasEllipsis, viewport

axes.name: Frequency-weighted thumb reach (Fitts ID)
axes.source: GlassCam_fixed/GlassCam/tools/critique/scorers.py:55 (shutter column); settings_scorers.py:172 (settings panel, scroll + chip cost); settings_scorers.py:213 (chips_reach); settings_compare.py:122 (measured reach_dp from uiautomator)
axes.definition: Controls used most should be cheapest to hit from the resting thumb: frequency-weighted Fitts index of difficulty from a thumb anchor, normalised against a worst case.

measurement.inputs: layout geometry (cell centres and widths in dp) from a model or probe JSON; per-control use frequency table (judgement declared as data)
measurement.formula: ID_i = log2(d_i/w_i + 1), d_i = |centre_i - THUMB|; reach = max(0, 1 - sum(f_i*ID_i) / sum(f_i*ID_worst)), ID_worst = log2(hypot(W,H)/24 + 1). Settings variant adds navigation cost nav = min(y/LIST_H, chip_cost + (y-sec_top)/LIST_H), cost = nav + ID/4, capped at worst = 6 + log2(hypot(W,H)/48+1). Measured variant: mean dp distance from thumb anchor to each top-level tappable centre.
measurement.range: [0,1] (clamped after fresh-eyes found negatives when cell < 24 dp)

axes.weighting: shutter layout reach 0.30 (+ strip_reach 0.15, a lookup bottom 1.0/left 0.55/top 0.35); settings panel reach 0.35 + chips_reach 0.10. Settings space (5,760 points) was exhaustively enumerated under two row-height models to check the decision holds for the shipped panel.
axes.validation: fresh-eyes 2026-09-28 found the settings model scored a panel never built (wrong header/row heights); now selectable row_model with uniform_76 measured from uiautomator dump.
axes.scifin_reason: Placement of Add/entry FAB and tab bar on a 360 dp portrait phone is exactly a frequency-weighted reach question; anchor must move to bottom-right portrait (and pointer, not thumb, on desktop).
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON rects + per-control frequency table (Add > tabs > settings) + portrait thumb anchor

axes.name: Type scale steps and size count
axes.definition: The scale uses few distinct sizes (<=5) with adjacent ratios close to a modular scale (1.2/1.25/1.333); unset M3 roles fall back to Roboto defaults.

measurement.inputs: Typography tokens (static) or text sizes from probe JSON
measurement.formula: Tendril: 1 if n_sizes <= 5 else max(0, 1 - (n-5)/2); mnemo: adjacent ratios vs designkit build_scale(base 14 sp, r in {1.2,1.25,1.333})

axes.scifin_reason: Sci-Fin hero balance vs list amounts vs captions; probe gives rendered sp.
axes.port_inputs: text sizes from probe JSON or Type.kt

axes.name: Type-scale regularity and sprawl
axes.definition: Whether the distinct font sizes in use follow one modular ratio, how many sizes exist, and how many font families.

measurement.formula: sorted distinct sizes -> step ratios r_i; for each known ratio R: err = mean |ln(r_i/R)|; best = argmin. Irregular if best_err > 0.09 (needs >=3 sizes). Sprawl if >7 distinct sizes; font sprawl if >3 families.

axes.scifin_reason: Computable straight from probe font sizes per screen; catches one-off sp values.
axes.port_inputs: Probe font sizes (sp or px) and families

axes.name: Accessibility semantics
axes.definition: Language and viewport declared, images have alt, icon-only controls have accessible names, inputs have labels, heading levels do not skip, single h1.

measurement.formula: Rule checks producing error/warn/note

axes.scifin_reason: The Compose equivalent: icon-only clickables need contentDescription, text fields need labels, headings need semantics heading(). Needs a semantics-tree dump in the probe.
axes.port_inputs: Compose semantics tree (role, contentDescription, text, heading flag) per probe node

axes.name: Display size cap
axes.definition: The largest heading must not exceed the medium's ceiling, so a high scale ratio cannot produce absurd display sizes.

measurement.formula: base*16*ratio^top_step <= max_display_px (typography.py:315)

axes.scifin_reason: Needs a phone-specific cap (for example a balance hero numeral in sp) checked against the measured largest font in the probe.
axes.port_inputs: Max font size per screen from the probe; per-form-factor cap.

axes.name: Unconsidered-default tells
axes.definition: Defaults that mark a design as unconsidered: a saturated purple-to-blue gradient, system-default typefaces only, everything centre-aligned. frontend-design adds the three AI-default looks (cream #F4F1EA + serif + terracotta #D97757; near-black + acid accent; hairline broadsheet).

measurement.formula: purple(255-300 deg) plus blue(200-255 deg) stops with sat>=0.3; families subset of {inter, system-ui, ...}; centred >= 5 and centred/blocks > 0.5. Labelled kind='judgement'.

axes.scifin_reason: A low-weight distinctiveness check; centre-alignment share and palette distance (dE) from the default looks are computable from probes.
axes.port_inputs: Probe text alignment and families; theme hexes

axes.name: Judgment / guilt marks in view
axes.definition: Count of marks in view that judge the person: streaks, percentages, 'n/m done', empty past cells, missed cells, amounts shown as a fraction under target. A calm, non-judgmental register was the owner's aim.

measurement.inputs: DOM: elements tagged data-judge or data-cell=miss above the bar; empty past dots; fractions below target
measurement.formula: guilt = empty_past_dots + miss_cells + fractions_under_target (+ every row for the control's streaks); judgment_marks = count([data-judge] visible above bar)

axes.aggregation: Own 'Judgment' axis or in 'Calm' in every T3 part.
axes.validation: Control (streak + percentage + seven days per row) loses.
axes.scifin_reason: Highly relevant to budgets/goals (over-budget red, '% spent', missed savings); Sci-Fin must tag which elements judge.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON with a 'judges' flag on elements (e.g. overspend badges, percent-of-goal, streaks)

axes.name: Kind separation (preattentive channels)
axes.definition: For each pair of item kinds shown, the share of three preattentive channels that differ: region (zone/lane/section), shape (height, width, radius, dash bucketed) and leading glyph. 1: every pair differs on all three.

measurement.inputs: DOM probe of items tagged with kind
measurement.formula: per kind modal (region, (h//12, round(w/360*4), radius, dash), glyph); kind_sep = mean over pairs of (#differing channels / 3); 0 if one kind

axes.scifin_reason: Income vs expense vs transfer vs scheduled rows told apart without relying on colour.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON rows with kind tag, bounds, corner radius, leading glyph id, container id

axes.name: Screen memory: safety (stale input, lost edits)
axes.definition: Arrivals showing input other than what the task needs (a chance to act on the wrong thing) plus unsaved edits discarded without asking, the latter weighted 3x ('lost work is worse than a wrong file you can see').

measurement.formula: harm = stale + 3*lost; s_safety = 1 - harm/worst harm

axes.validation: as above
axes.scifin_fit_reason: Stale prefilled account/amount on an entry form is a money-correctness risk; same weighting idea.
axes.port_inputs: as above
axes.fit_reason: Stale prefilled account/amount on an entry form is a money-correctness risk; same weighting idea.

axes.name: Recovery: one-tap writes
axes.definition: Share of logs (frequency-weighted) written by a single tap with no confirming step: the cost of an accidental write.

measurement.formula: oneshot_freq / logged_freq

axes.scifin_reason: Quick-add of recurring expenses; in money, one-tap writes are riskier, so weigh against taps.
axes.port_inputs: declared entry paths + frequencies

axes.name: Progressive disclosure (section order)
axes.definition: Whether the section order follows the canonical given-to-new sequence for the content type and honours declared precedence, must-lead and must-trail rules.

measurement.formula: Kendall agreement = 1 - discordant/(n(n-1)/2) over shared items (layout.py:130), weight 0.5; rule hits/checks, weight 0.5 (1.0 if there is no canonical sequence). must_lead: pos < max(1, ceil(n/3)); must_trail: pos >= n - max(1, ceil(n/3)). Nothing declared -> 0.6.

axes.scifin_reason: Works on probe section ids once Sci-Fin declares a canonical order per screen type (overview, budget, transactions).
axes.port_inputs: Vertical order of section ids from the layout probe; per-screen canonical list and rules.

axes.name: App-register layout fitness (aggregate)
axes.definition: Weighted sum of the four base layout components plus register_fit. Registerless screens use the base four weights.

measurement.formula: fitness = sum(w_k * score_k)

constants.skill_md_weights: PD 0.2875, EC 0.2375, CL 0.1375, MF 0.1150, RF 0.20 (SKILL.md:150), which does not match the code

axes.scifin_reason: The aggregate is usable, but the four base components need probe-derived inputs (see below). The weight discrepancy between SKILL.md and the code has to be resolved first.
axes.port_inputs: The five component scores.

axes.name: Space used across plausible sizes (breakpoint coverage)
axes.definition: Across a weighted set of sizes a person plausibly gives the surface, how much of the room renders the richest content tier that fits; plus: the floor size renders something (gate), and every declared breakpoint changes what is shown.

measurement.inputs: content tiers (min w/h dp, label, node count), placement priors (size -> weight), declared floor/ceiling/breakpoints; actual cell 78x95 dp vs declared 70n-30
measurement.formula: coverage per surface = sum w_p * max(0, 1 - (ideal_tier - shown_tier)/max_tier) (0 below floor, 0.45 above ceiling); aggregate 0.7*mean + 0.3*min. min_legible = 1 if tier0 fits at floor else 0.5*shortfall. info_gain = 0.6*captured_tiers/available + 0.4*distinct_tiers/breakpoints.

axes.weighting: min_legible 0.22, coverage 0.22, info_gain 0.20, spec_fit 0.14, effort 0.12, payload 0.10
axes.validation: sensitivity.py sweep; docstrings record three reward hacks found and closed (raising floors bought fitness; plain mean let one widget be sacrificed; info_gain vs own box let ceilings shrink).
axes.scifin_reason: Maps to Sci-Fin phone 360 dp -> desktop window widths: does each breakpoint (compact/medium/expanded) actually show more (e.g. budget + chart side by side)? Glance/RemoteViews payload term does not carry unless Sci-Fin ships widgets.
axes.port_inputs: content tiers per screen with min widths, window-size priors, breakpoint list; probe JSON at each width

axes.name: Lookup cost in reading order
axes.definition: Readables (items, hour labels, section headers) the eye passes to answer 'what is at 09:00'; if the reading order is not in time order, every readable counts.

measurement.inputs: DOM readables with y, x, time
measurement.formula: order by (y//8, x); if times monotone cost = index+1 else len(order); mean over targets

axes.scifin_reason: Finding a transaction by date in the ledger, or a bill in an upcoming list.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON readables with key (date/amount) and bounds

axes.name: Titles cut / legible share / title room
axes.definition: Titles clipped (scrollWidth > clientWidth), the readable share of each title (whole, unbroken, unclipped words over all its words), and the mean width a title has left after labels/actions.

measurement.inputs: DOM text boxes vs their overflow
measurement.formula: cut = count(scrollWidth > clientWidth + 1); legible = mean(chars_readable/total); title_room = mean title width px

axes.aggregation: Density / Legibility / Calm axes; 'no title cut' as a gate in T3 measure2.
axes.validation: legible_share replaced raw characters, which favoured views with longer visible titles.
axes.scifin_reason: Payee names and amounts truncating on 360 dp; probe must expose text overflow (Compose TextLayoutResult.hasVisualOverflow).

axes.name: Later text never louder than the block's first
axes.definition: Within a block, a later Text is never larger or heavier than the first one.

measurement.inputs: text sites with block key and index (type_sites inventory; or probe JSON children order)
measurement.formula: ok/pairs where ok = size_later <= size_first and weight_later <= weight_first

axes.scifin_reason: Budget card: title > amount? Sci-Fin may deliberately make the amount louder than the label - needs an exemption class for money figures.
axes.port_inputs: probe JSON text nodes with parent container + style

axes.name: Title vs body type ratio (1f, first half)
axes.definition: Whether the page title stands above body text by the type ramp's intended size and weight ratios. Polish version: boolean 'the largest font on screen is within the top 60 px'.

measurement.inputs: widget dump: font_px and weight per text leaf, title widget identified
measurement.formula: body_px, body_wt = modal size/weight of non-title labels; r = title_px/body_px, q = title_wt/body_wt; parts = 100*min(r/2.0, 2.0/r), 100*min(q/1.5, 1.5/q)

axes.validation: none beyond the run

axes.fit_reason: Retarget ratios to Material 3 (e.g. headlineSmall 24 / bodyLarge 16 = 1.5); Sci-Fin may want the hero money figure, not the title, as the largest text.

axes.name: UX copy: weak CTAs and empty error copy
axes.definition: Button labels that name the mechanism ('Submit', 'OK', 'Next') instead of the outcome, and error copy that apologises without explaining. Same principle in frontend-design SKILL.md:62-66.

measurement.formula: lowercased, punctuation stripped, label in WEAK_CTA set -> note; any EMPTY_ERROR phrase in text -> note

constants.WEAK_CTA: submit, click here, learn more, continue, ok, next, save, confirm, ...
constants.EMPTY_ERROR: something went wrong, an error occurred, oops, unknown error, failed, ...

notes.factotum: Scope: tools/screens/*.py (55 files, ~17.5k lines; the inventory lists none of them as duplicated), tools/score_contest.py, docs/screens/t0/nav-glance.md, docs/screens/t1/scores.md and docs/screens/t0/reference-protocol.md. Nothing was run. Method shared across the group: every screen part is an enumerated design space, rendered in headless Edge at 360x740 (phone) and 1100x660 (Windows), in light and dark. Each variant is measured with the same JS probe (screen_score.MEASURE_JS) and the same pixel metrics, then ranked by Pareto front or by rank sums per axis (Borda: capture_v2.ranks averages ties inside per-measure tolerances, and an axis sums its measures' ranks, or takes the worse rank with 'max:' keys). The front is taken over the axes. There are no hand weights, except palette_personality_score at 0.45/0.35/0.20. Constraints act as gates: 48 dp targets, no title cut, 0 hidden, over_box 0, owner rules. In T3 one measure can lead (T.LEAD): fewest taps, with a 0.17-0.25 tolerance. VALIDATION PATTERN worth porting: every part has a deliberately bad control, and the run fails (exit 2, or 'The control is on the front: the measures are not discriminating') if the control is not beaten. Clutter is also calibrated against real apps' screenshots (0.011 to 0.079 at 360 px wide) and checked for threshold robustness. Measurement bugs found and fixed: (1) headless --dump-dom laid out at 492x648 whatever --window-size said, which falsely hid targets, so pages are now measured in a larger window; (2) position-only visibility counted cut-off cards as seen, so it is now hit-tested; (3) cold browser launches held the CPU at 100% on a 10k-option run, so cdp.py now keeps one browser per worker and a partial jsonl resumes stopped runs. Superseded or merged: nav_score.py (job costs, 2026-10-05) into nav_score2; nav_glance 'primary' into strong_targets; title_edges and capture 'edges' into alignment_edges; sheet_weight mass, capture_v2 emphasis, picker 'heavy', hub header share and alarm dismiss_pull into visual_mass_emphasis; the various cover_px, banner_px, block_px and sheet_h into covered_share. Not catalogued as screen axes (too domain-specific): shorthand token clash (shorthands.py), legend readable-count (legend_opt), repeat-rule coverage (repeat_opt), cron and picker-specific task sets, and the purpose_map checks (structural lints). For Sci-Fin, most DOM-based axes need a Compose probe that provides bounds in dp, a clickable/role flag, text colour and resolved background, font size, a text-overflow flag and z-order/overlay membership. Pixel axes (clutter, mass, empty_share, focal) need only the PNG at known density, scaled to 360 dp wide.
